newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas says union reaches pact.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas says union reaches pact.

text.p: Defense contractor McDonnell Douglas Corp said it reached a tentative agreement with the International Association of Machinists -- a deal that could end a three-month strike at a St. Louis-based jet fighter factory.
"We're very hopeful that this (tentative agreement) will be the end of the strike," Tom Williams, vice president of communications at the company, said in a telephone interview.
Terms were not disclosed for the deal that would affect 6,700 union members.
Williams expects the union to vote on the tentative deal sometime next week. Williams said engineers and other white collar employees have been working on the factory since the strike began June 5.
"We've been keeping up production of fighter aircraft, but it's been a strain on the company," Williams said.
The company has delivered 60 missiles and 13 aircraft while the union was on strike, which is slightly below the company's normal production rate, the company said.

The strike was against McDonnell Douglas's site in St. Louis, where it makes the F-15, F-18, Harrier and T-45 aircraft, as well as Harpoon and SLAM missiles, and performs some assembly work for the C-17 cargo aircraft.
On August 16, union officials halted contract talks, saying the company was unwilling to bargain on job security.
The negotiations that led to the tentative agreement were conducted by the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.
